metadata.title: Odin OS: Cryptographically Authorized Memory Mutation in a RISC-V PMP-Enforced Agent Execution Environment
metadata.description:
Odin OS (Phase B.3.2 Publication Release Candidate) is a bare-metal, zero-allocation (#![no_std]) 64-bit RISC-V microkernel that anchors autonomous AI agent capability boundaries in processor Physical Memory Protection (PMP) comparators. Operating on the central axiom that state which cannot prove its right to exist cannot be committed to memory or disk, Odin OS enforces capability containment via cache-line aligned 256-byte binary tokens termed TransitionDeeds.

Enforcement Boundary: Spatial PEP vs. Semantic PDP

Odin OS operates strictly as a hardware-enforced Policy Enforcement Point (PEP). It enforces spatial memory confinement (where stores can occur) and temporal containment (when leases are valid). Crucially, the PEP is agnostic to business semantics: it verifies cryptographic rights to access physical memory, not whether a business mutation makes application-level sense. Upstream semantic authorization is delegated to the independent Policy Decision Point (PDP).

Primary Falsifiable Claim for Independent Reviewers

Under an untrusted U-Mode agent executing arbitrary instructions, no memory store instruction can retire to any physical memory location outside the explicitly signed [lease_start, lease_end) window or after revocation without triggering an architectural CPU access fault (mcause = 7) that aborts the write and leaves target memory unmodified.

Included Release Artifacts

  • odin-os-whitepaper.pdf: Complete 6-page publication manuscript including the Claim-to-Evidence mapping, PMP memory layout, formal assurance theorems, and limitations.
  • empirical-receipts.txt: Clean empirical trace of the 17-case QEMU adversarial matrix and live Gemma 4 jailbreak deflection bridge.
  • odin-os-v0.1.0-src.tar.gz: Complete open-source distribution containing Rust microkernel source, linker scripts, Z3 formal SMT proofs, mutation testing harnesses, and automated release verifiers (make verify-release).
